theme.event_line: 20 Years of Impact · Rising to a New Era

presenter.talking_point: Assalamu Alaikum. Before we begin, I want to ask a simple question: are we truly happy? MBF has spent 20 years growing and serving. Tonight, let’s think about what actually makes a good life.
presenter.transition: Let’s start by hearing from the room.

steps.title: If you could choose only ONE, what is most important for a truly happy life?

presenter.talking_point: Before we get into the topic, I want your answer. If you could pick only one, what matters most for a happy life? There’s no right answer. Scan the code and choose honestly.
presenter.transition: Okay, let’s see what we chose.

presenter.talking_point: That’s interesting. Don’t read too much into it yet—just remember this result. We’ll come back to the same question near the end.
presenter.transition: Now think back over the last 20 years.

steps.title: Compared with 20 years ago, are people generally happier today?

config.eyebrow: MORE TECHNOLOGY · MORE INFORMATION · MORE CONVENIENCE

presenter.talking_point: A lot has changed in 20 years. We have better technology, faster communication, and more convenience. But are people actually happier now? What do you think?
presenter.transition: Let’s look beyond our opinions for a moment.

steps.title: What Makes a Good Life?
steps.subtitle: Harvard Study of Adult Development · Started in 1938

presenter.talking_point: Harvard has followed people’s lives since 1938. They wanted to understand what really helps people live well. Here’s one lesson they found.
presenter.transition: That study says relationships matter. As Muslims, we have to take the question one step further.

steps.title: Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort.

config.translation: Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort.

presenter.talking_point: For us, the good life starts with Allah. The Qur’an tells us that hearts find rest in remembering Him. And our faith teaches us to care for others as we care for ourselves. Faith and relationships belong together.
presenter.action_cue: Slow down · Leave the verse visible
presenter.transition: Here’s a simple way to picture that.

steps.title: The connection framework
steps.subtitle: Faith grounds the individual. Strong relationships turn belief into service.

nodes.label: SERVICE & PURPOSE
nodes.caption: Live with meaning. Serve with impact.

presenter.talking_point: It starts with Allah, then it shapes us. From there it reaches our families, our brothers and sisters, and the wider community. And it should lead to service—not stop with us.

steps.title: How many people outside your household could you call at 2:00 AM?

presenter.talking_point: Imagine you really need help at 2:00 in the morning. Outside your home, who could you call and know they would come through? Be honest—it’s anonymous. We may have hundreds of contacts, but how many real relationships do we have?
presenter.action_cue: Open voting · Pause when results appear
presenter.transition: Let’s do something about that right now.

steps.title: MBF Connection Challenge
steps.subtitle: Find someone you don’t know well.

prompts: What are you grateful to Allah for this year?
What do you hope to gain from this Summit?
What could our community do better?

presenter.talking_point: Please stand up and find someone you don’t know well—not the person you came with. Use the questions on screen. You have three minutes. And try to remember their name tomorrow.
presenter.action_cue: Start the 3-minute timer · Help people pair up
presenter.transition: Welcome back. That small conversation is how community starts.

steps.title: Which relationship needs the most attention in our Muslim community today?

presenter.talking_point: Being in the same building doesn’t automatically make us a community. Relationships take effort. Where do you think we need the most work right now?

steps.title: Twenty years from now, what would make us say MBF truly succeeded?

presenter.talking_point: Picture MBF 20 years from now. What would make us say we really succeeded? Choose up to three. This isn’t just for the screen—your answers tell us what the community wants us to prioritize.
presenter.transition: Now say that future in just one word.

steps.title: In ONE word, what should describe the MBF community 20 years from now?

presenter.talking_point: One word only: what should describe MBF 20 years from now?
presenter.action_cue: Open the word cloud · Stay quiet for 10–15 seconds, then read a few large words
presenter.transition: Keep those words in mind. Let’s return to our first question.
presenter.private_notes: Give the room time to watch the words appear.

steps.title: If you could choose only ONE, what is most important for a truly happy life?

presenter.talking_point: Here’s the same question again. After our conversation, what would you choose now? There’s still no answer you’re supposed to pick.
presenter.action_cue: Open voting · Keep the wording unchanged

presenter.talking_point: Here are the two results side by side. What changed? Call out only the shifts that are easy to see. We’re not proving that this conversation caused them—we’re just noticing what moved.
presenter.action_cue: Show comparison · Keep the interpretation simple
presenter.transition: So, what might the good life look like for us?

presenter.talking_point: So what have we learned? A good life isn’t only about comfort or success. It starts with faith. It grows through family and brotherhood. It finds purpose in serving others. Jazakumullahu khairan for taking part. Twenty years brought us here. Bismillah—let’s begin the MBF Summit 2026.
presenter.action_cue: Pause briefly · Move directly into the program
presenter.private_notes: If animation is available, reveal the five words one at a time.
